ui.artist_subtitle: The master of guerrilla sculpture and mini statues
ui.artist_bio_text: Mihály Kolodko was born in 1978 in Uzhhorod, Ukraine. He graduated in sculpture from the Lviv Academy of Arts. Initially, he created monumental public statues, then found his way to the world of mini statues. In 2017, he moved with his family to Vác, Hungary, which is when his first iconic Budapest creations appeared and quickly stole the hearts of the city's residents.
ui.artist_style_text: His works are characterized by subtle humor, irony, and a deep respect for pop culture. Whether it involves cartoon characters (Chief Worm, Checkered-Eared Rabbit), historical figures, or the little oddities of everyday life, his statues always reflect on the location and society. Despite their miniature size, the statues are incredibly detailed and expressive.
ui.artist_guerilla_text: The essence of guerrilla sculpture is the magic of freedom and surprise. He often places his creations in public spaces without prior permission or announcement, usually under the cover of night. This type of art creates a direct, playful connection with passers-by, who can discover the hidden artworks around the city like treasure hunters.
ui.artist_craft_text: Each of his statues is individually made using traditional lost-wax bronze casting. During the process, the highly detailed wax model is cast into a mold, melted out, and then 1200-degree liquid bronze is poured in its place. After cooling, the statue is cleaned, patinated, and polished to its final form.
ui.artist_locations_text: Although Budapest has undoubtedly become the 'capital' of Kolodko mini statues, his creations can be found in many other places. Many mini statues decorate the streets of his hometown, Uzhhorod, but you can also encounter them in Veszprém, Vác, Tihany, and even beyond the borders in Munich, Rijeka, and Pula.
ui.artist_education_text: His artistic interest led him to the Adalbert Erdeli College of Arts in Uzhhorod, and in 2002 he graduated from the sculpture department of the Lviv Academy of Arts. Initially interested in monumental sculpture, he practiced his studies in plein air art. He created his first public statues in his hometown, including the Lamplighter erected in 2010, which commemorates a real local character.
ui.artist_awards_text: Although the essence of guerrilla art is anonymity and the avoidance of formal frameworks, Kolodko's work has now gained international recognition. His statues have become important drivers of urban tourism and public art. He has also participated in initiatives supporting educational and environmental projects (such as the 'Concrete Sharks' in Vác made jointly with Duna-Dráva Cement, which drew attention to waste recycling and won a PREXA bronze award).
